stances_toward.note: Jubaland is Kenya's buffer and its client: Kenyan peacekeepers have been accused since 2013 of building a buffer state around Kismayo, Jubaland fighters beaten at Balad Hawo in 2021 fled to Mandera and Jubaland troops were reported there again in 2026 (SOM card), and Nairobi is accused of keeping Madobe in power; it denies arming militias (Kenya government spokesman, 2021). Graded partner and not ally because no treaty or public commitment exists and Nairobi still deals with Mogadishu as the sovereign it hosts troops for; not rival because it never opposes Jubaland. The Somali card reads the same pair from the other side as rival (Mogadishu toward Kismayo), so the seam between federal host and local client runs through Nairobi. Confidence C: every source is an accusation or a denial; Kenya has never stated the backing. Trend stable: the 2026 loss of three Gedo towns by federal forces strengthens Madobe without Kenya acting. Bond none: interest.

stances_toward.note: Jubaland rejected the March 2026 constitutional amendments (AllAfrica, 4 Mar 2026) and by 10 Oct 2026 had retaken Balad Hawo from federal troops who had taken it months earlier (the article gives no date); it now holds Balad Hawo, Dolow, Luuq and El Wak while federal-aligned forces hold Bardere and Garbaharey (Somali Guardian, 10 Oct 2026). Mogadishu's tool was a parallel administration in Gedo, a 45-day plan of October 2025 that Ethiopia called a direct threat to its security; Kenya has backed Madobe for over a decade and Jubaland troops were again reported at Mandera in 2026 (see the Kenya stance). Graded rival and not claimed_territory for the reason given for Puntland (the Kismayo administration is the actor, the land stays Somali in Mogadishu's reading). Cooling: the federal government lost three towns in 48 hours to its rivals in the second week of October. The since-date is that of the rejection cited; the Gedo dispute is older (the parallel-administration plan is of October 2025, Kenya's backing of Madobe older still) and no earlier source was read. Bond kin, as for Puntland. The Jubaland-side reading was not found, so the reciprocal stance is provisional.
